reasoning: The question asks if a Russian crewed aircraft will be shot down in NATO airspace by March 19, 2026 (13 days from the forecast date of March 6, 2026). Historical precedent: Turkey shot down a Russian Su-24 in 2015. Recent context: Russian aircraft violated Estonian airspace in September 2025 but were only escorted out. The 13-day window is very short. While tensions exist, actual shootdowns are rare despite frequent violations. The 2015 incident was exceptional. Current NATO rules of engagement typically involve interception and escort rather than shooting down. The probability of an escalation to actual combat in this narrow timeframe is low.
